topic: Hip fracture care standards (national audit and best practice tariff)

audits.title: 258 RISING TO THE CHALLENGE: ORTHOGERIATRIC SERVICE IMPROVEMENT AND COVID-19
audits.standard: Irish Hip Fracture Standards 1-6 (Irish Hip Fracture Database)
audits.setting: Our Lady of Lourdes Hospital, Drogheda, hip fracture patients over 60

cycle1.result: Admitted to orthopaedic ward within 4 hours 56%; surgery within 48 hours 60%; pressure ulcers 2%; IHFS4-6 98%; all IHFS met in 32%.

audits.intervention: Hip Fracture Pathway Subgroup, IHFS1 breaches audit, orthogeriatric input at orthopaedic inductions, weekly MDT meetings, nutritional hip fracture pathway and a Fracture Liaison Service ANP.

cycle2.result: Ward within 4 hours 71%; surgery within 48 hours 66%; pressure ulcers 3%; IHFS4-6 87%; all IHFS met in 43%.

audits.other_findings: Lower IHFS4-6 in 2020 reflected COVID-19 redeployment of the orthogeriatric service and MDT; €90,000 Best Practice Tariff funding achieved.
audits.citation: Stankard A, Thomas N, Cosgrave N, Conlon B, Monaghan P, Halpin T, et al.. 258 RISING TO THE CHALLENGE: ORTHOGERIATRIC SERVICE IMPROVEMENT AND COVID-19. Age and Ageing. 2022;51(Supplement_3). doi:10.1093/ageing/afac218.227.

audits.title: Quality improvement for patients with hip fracture: experience from a multi-site audit.
audits.standard: Indicator standards for re-audit circulated after the 1992 audit
audits.setting: Seven hospitals with trauma orthopaedic departments, East Anglia (multi-site audit)
audits.intervention: Results of the 1992 audit and indicator standards circulated to orthopaedic and care of the elderly consultants and audit leads at each hospital.

cycle2.result: Pharmaceutical thromboembolic prophylaxis 81%; early mobilisation 70%; reduced pneumonia, wound infection, pressure sores and fatal PE.

audits.other_findings: No change in 3-month functional outcome or mortality; some hospitals failed to maintain good practice.
audits.citation: Freeman C, Todd C, Camilleri-Ferrante C, Laxton C, Murrell P, Palmer CR, et al.. Quality improvement for patients with hip fracture: experience from a multi-site audit. Qual Saf Health Care. 2002;11(3):239-245. doi:10.1136/qhc.11.3.239. PMID: 12486988.

audits.title: Improvements in pain relief, handling time and pressure ulcers through internal audits of hip fracture patients.
audits.standard: Aims: optimise preoperative pain relief, reduce time from admission to operation and reduce pressure ulcers; no target stated
audits.setting: Department of Orthopedics, Lund University Hospital

cycle1.result: Close to half waited more than 24 hours for operation; 11% operated within 12 hours; 19% had pressure ulcers at discharge

audits.intervention: Quality improvements with attention from all staff (details not given)

cycle2.result: 34% waited more than 24 hours; 24% operated within 12 hours; 4.5% had pressure ulcers at discharge

audits.other_findings: Interim 1999 measurement: 36% waited more than 24 hours, 18% operated within 12 hours, 8% pressure ulcers. Patients waiting more than 1 hour for pain relief almost halved.
audits.citation: Hommel A, Ulander K, Thorngren KG. Improvements in pain relief, handling time and pressure ulcers through internal audits of hip fracture patients. Scand J Caring Sci. 2003;17(1):78-83. doi:10.1046/j.1471-6712.2003.00212.x. PMID: 12581299.

audits.title: The national clinical audit of falls and bone health: the clinical management of hip fracture patients.
audits.standard: Published national guidelines for hip fracture care in older people
audits.setting: All acute trusts admitting orthopaedic trauma and all primary care trusts in England

cycle1.result: A&E stay under 2h 20% (640/3133) and over 240 min 23%; surgery within 24h 35% (1080/3088); sat out of bed within 24h 48% (1480/2998); orthogeriatric care 35% (1115/3184); median stay 16 days.

audits.other_findings: Delays to theatre were due to awaiting medical review (59%, 566/956) or organisational reasons (29%, 278/956).
audits.citation: Youde J, Husk J, Lowe D, Grant R, Potter J, Martin F. The national clinical audit of falls and bone health: the clinical management of hip fracture patients. Injury. 2009;40(11):1226-1230. doi:10.1016/j.injury.2009.06.167. PMID: 19647251.

audits.title: Auckland City Hospital's Ortho-Geriatric Service: an audit of patients aged over 65 with fractured neck of femur.
audits.standard: ANZHFR Minimum Data Set and NICE hip fracture guidelines; national health target of ED admission within 6 hours

cycle1.result: 76% admitted from ED within 6 hours; 86% had surgery within 48 hours; 82% had rehabilitation by Older People's Health; bisphosphonates prescribed for 56%.

audits.other_findings: Timely surgery improved significantly compared with 2007 hospital data; inpatient and 30-day mortality 5%, 120-day mortality 15%; osteoporosis assessment and treatment need attention.
audits.citation: Wimalasena B, Harris R. Auckland City Hospital's Ortho-Geriatric Service: an audit of patients aged over 65 with fractured neck of femur. N Z Med J. 2016;129(1437):15-26. PMID: 27362595.

audits.title: Audit of standards of practice in suspected hip fracture.
audits.standard: Standards from national policies and evidence-based literature: early analgesia, accurate clinical assessment, prompt transfer to orthopaedic ward
audits.setting: Emergency Department (University of Nottingham affiliation); ED Information System records

cycle1.result: Good performance on medical assessment; shortfalls in pressure-care assessment, timely ward transfer and pain relief (figures not given in abstract).

audits.other_findings: Authors recommend a care bundle for pain relief, pressure care and fast-tracking.

audits.title: Implementing the National Hip Fracture Database: An audit of care.
audits.setting: Department of Trauma and Orthopaedic Surgery, Kingston Hospital

cycle1.period: First six months after NHFD introduction
cycle1.result: Overall (both periods, n=372): median time to surgery 24.5 h, 251 (67.5%) within 36 h; median length of stay 11 days; inpatient mortality 6.2%.

audits.intervention: Implementation of the National Hip Fracture Database.

cycle2.result: More patients assessed by an orthogeriatrician, with shorter time to surgery and length of stay (period figures not given in the supplied text).

audits.other_findings: Surgical delay was mainly for medical reasons (54.7%) and lack of theatre space (37.6%).
audits.citation: Patel NK, Sarraf KM, Joseph S, Lee C, Middleton FR. Implementing the National Hip Fracture Database: An audit of care. Injury. 2013;44(12):1934-1939. doi:10.1016/j.injury.2013.04.012. PMID: 23680283.

audits.title: The Best Practice Tariff helps improve management of neck of femur fractures: a completed audit loop.
audits.standard: Best Practice Tariff 2010-11 targets, including surgery within 36 hours and geriatrician review within 72 hours
audits.setting: James Cook University Hospital, Middlesbrough (regional major trauma centre)

cycle1.result: Surgery within 36 hours 48.3%; geriatric review within 72 hours 68.8%.

audits.intervention: A series of procedural and logistical measures (details not given in abstract).

cycle2.result: Surgery within 36 hours 73.4%; geriatric review within 72 hours 81.8%.

audits.other_findings: Thirty-day mortality compared using the summary hospital-level mortality indicator.

audits.title: Management of hip fractures in older people in Beijing: a retrospective audit and comparison with evidence-based guidelines and practice in the UK.
audits.standard: UK Blue Book standards, compared with National Hip Fracture Database 2012 (180 UK hospitals)

cycle1.result: 66% admitted to orthopaedic ward within 24 h; 8% surgery within 48 h (UK 83%); 10% no surgery; 27% orthogeriatric assessment (UK 70%); 0.3% osteoporosis assessment (UK 94%); 3.8% falls assessment (UK 92%)

audits.title: National audits of hip fractures: Are yearly audits required?
audits.standard: Scottish hip fracture clinical standards including discharge from A&E within 4 h and surgery within 48 h of admission
audits.setting: Scottish Hip Fracture Audit and MSK Hip Fracture Audit, participating Scottish hospitals

cycle1.result: Discharge from A&E within 4 h improved from 80.5% (2003) to 96% (2008); surgery within 48 h improved from 89.9% to 98.4%.

audits.intervention: Continuous annual audit discontinued in 2008, then re-introduced in 2014

cycle2.result: A&E 4 h improvement not maintained; surgery within 48 h fell to 91.8%.

audits.other_findings: 30-day mortality improved and kept improving in 2013; re-introduction of continuous audit in 2014 improved A&E waits and time to theatre again.
audits.citation: Ferguson KB, Halai M, Winter A, Elswood T, Smith R, Hutchison JD, et al.. National audits of hip fractures: Are yearly audits required?. Injury. 2016;47(2):439-443. doi:10.1016/j.injury.2015.11.018. PMID: 26657888.

audits.title: Improving inpatient care with the introduction of a hip fracture pathway.
audits.standard: National Hip Fracture Database best practice tariff criteria (surgery within 36 h, orthogeriatric review within 72 h, pre- and post-operative AMT, etc.)
audits.setting: University College London Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust; acute hip fracture service

cycle1.result: BPT achieved in 8/18 (44.4%); 4 waited >36 h for surgery, 7 >72 h for orthogeriatric review, 9 lacked both AMT scores; FI block in ED 3/18 (16.7%)

audits.intervention: Eight-page multidisciplinary clerking booklet, hip fracture care group, twice-weekly consultant orthogeriatric ward rounds, and booklet in local induction

cycle2.result: BPT achieved in 22/24 (91.7%); all had both AMT scores; FI block in ED in 6

audits.other_findings: Booklet used in 27/30 (90%) but ED section complete in only 20 (74.1%); mean acute stay fell from 18.9 to 16.4 days (p=0.066).
audits.citation: Chamberlain M, Pugh H. Improving inpatient care with the introduction of a hip fracture pathway. BMJ Qual Improv Rep. 2015;4(1):u204075.w2786. doi:10.1136/bmjquality.u204075.w2786. PMID: 26734354.

audits.title: Reducing mortality from hip fractures: a systematic quality improvement programme.
audits.standard: Blue Book standards and hip fracture best practice tariff (including time to theatre within 36 hours), tracked via NHFD
audits.setting: St Peter's Hospital, Ashford & St Peter's NHS Trust, orthogeriatric hip fracture service

cycle1.result: 39.6% operated within 36 hours (2010); best practice tariff attainment 28% (2010); 30-day mortality 7.8%

audits.intervention: Integrated orthogeriatricians; LEAN (EQuIP) pathway redesign with split weekend theatre lists, priority theatre pyramid, new clerking proforma with falls and bone health, A-Z preoperative guide, fast bleep, extra pressure mattresses, seven-day physiotherapy, monthly governance meetings, and measures to prevent post-operative complications and improve Wednesday-admission review

cycle2.result: 84% operated within 36 hours (national 71%); best practice tariff attainment 83% (national 55%); 30-day mortality 5.3% (national 8.2%)

audits.other_findings: Peak results in 2012 were 88% within 36 hours and 88% BPT. Pressure ulcers fell from 5.4% to 3.2%, mobilisation within 24 hours rose from 41% to 75%, and Wednesday-admission mortality fell from 9.2% to 1.69%.
audits.citation: Lisk R, Yeong K. Reducing mortality from hip fractures: a systematic quality improvement programme. BMJ Qual Improv Rep. 2014;3(1):u205006.w2103. doi:10.1136/bmjquality.u205006.w2103. PMID: 27493729.

audits.title: The Introduction of a Multidisciplinary Hip Fracture Pathway to Optimise Patient Care and Reduce Mortality: A Prospective Audit of 161 Patients.
audits.standard: Cycle 1: Best Practice Tariff time to orthogeriatric assessment <72 hours and time to surgery <36 hours. Cycle 2: 100% preoperative medical assessment, orthogeriatric assessment <24 hours, time to surgery <36 hours
audits.setting: Chelsea & Westminster NHS Foundation Trust, London; district general hospital

cycle1.result: Preoperative medical assessment 19%; mean time to orthogeriatric assessment 91 hours; mean time to surgery 37 hours; mean length of stay 24.8 days; inpatient mortality 14%.

audits.intervention: New multidisciplinary hip fracture pathway from 1 June 2011: direct admission to the acute medical ward under joint named medical and orthopaedic consultants, anaesthetic assessment within 12 hours, consultant orthopaedic and orthogeriatric review within 24 hours; seminars and laminated posters for staff.

cycle2.result: Preoperative medical assessment 85% (p=0.0001); mean time to orthogeriatric assessment 19 hours (p=0.0001); mean time to surgery 31 hours (p=0.0663); length of stay 19.5 days (p=0.029); mortality 4% (p=0.0336).

audits.other_findings: Return to original accommodation rose from 57% to 80% (p=0.0069), and delays over 36 hours due to inadequate medical optimisation fell from 41% to 17%. The main remaining cause of breaches was lack of morning trauma lists, since rescheduled.
audits.citation: Shenouda M, Silk Z, Radha S, Bouanem E, Radford W. The Introduction of a Multidisciplinary Hip Fracture Pathway to Optimise Patient Care and Reduce Mortality: A Prospective Audit of 161 Patients. Open Orthop J. 2017;11:309-315. doi:10.2174/1874325001711010309. PMID: 28567160.

audits.title: The positive impact of a quality improvement collaborative on process indicators for geriatric hip fracture care.
audits.standard: Adherence to 23 quality indicators for geriatric hip fracture care
audits.setting: Quality improvement collaborative across 19 hospitals in Flanders

cycle1.result: Lowest adherence: nerve blocks 8.0%, steroids 9.7%, tranexamic acid 22.2%.

audits.intervention: Anonymous benchmarking fed back to centres and three educative sessions on specific topics.

cycle2.result: Nerve blocks 25.4%, steroids 26.4%, tranexamic acid 30.7% (significant improvement).

audits.other_findings: 1044 patients were included across both retrospective audits.
audits.citation: Coeckelberghs E, Seys D, Lens C, Vanhaecht K, Claessens F, Weltens C, et al.. The positive impact of a quality improvement collaborative on process indicators for geriatric hip fracture care. Arch Osteoporos. 2025;20(1):22. doi:10.1007/s11657-025-01504-9. PMID: 39937317.

audits.title: The development and evolution of the Irish Hip Fracture Database: a quality care initiative 2013-2024.
audits.standard: Irish Hip Fracture Standards (seven core clinical standards, 2017; based on BOA/BGS Blue Book standards) and best practice tariff criteria; data quality target of 90% case submission
audits.setting: Irish Hip Fracture Database national clinical audit, all 16 eligible acute hospitals in Ireland (NOCA, RCSI)

cycle1.result: Geriatrician assessment 11%, bone health assessment 65%, falls assessment 62%, surgery within 48 h 70%, admission from ED to orthopaedic ward 15%; national coverage 63%.

audits.intervention: Establishment of the national audit with governance committee, audit manager, hospital hip fracture governance committees, quarterly dashboards with SPC charts, a QI foundation programme, a best practice tariff (€1000 per compliant case, from 2018), the Golden Hip Award, and new orthogeriatric and advanced nurse practitioner posts.

cycle2.result: Geriatrician assessment 86%, bone health assessment 90%, falls assessment 87%, surgery within 48 h 77%, admission from ED to orthopaedic ward 36%; national coverage 95%; day one physiotherapy mobilisation 74% (2018) to 85%.

audits.other_findings: Total 41,304 cases 2013–2024; best practice tariff compliance rose from 7% (2018) to 21% (2024) and time to surgery remained the hardest standard to meet. Inpatient mortality fell from 5% to 4% and new long-term care admission from 6% to 3%.
audits.citation: Brent L, Ahern E, Murphy T, Hurson C, Coughlan T, Hickey P, et al.. The development and evolution of the Irish Hip Fracture Database: a quality care initiative 2013-2024. Arch Osteoporos. 2026;21(1):96. doi:10.1007/s11657-026-01731-8. PMID: 42342903.
